 This Petition Coming On For Preliminary Hearing,
This Day, The Court Made The Following:
 Order

1. The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a. "Issue a writ or direction or order writ in the nature of Certiorari, quashing the impugned endorsement dated 15.04.2023 in No.SamKam/ViBhuswaA/
MuMaRaiLei/01/09-10/35 vide Annexure- H. b.

Issue a writ or direction or order writ in the nature of Mandamus, directing the Respondents to pass the General Award under the New Act, 2013, guntas situated at Ravudakunda village, Tq:
Sindhanur, Dist: Raichur.

And c. Pass any such order or orders as deemed fit by this Hon'ble Court under the facts and circumstances of the case in the interest of justice and equity."
2.
The petitioner claims to be the owner of the land in Sy.No.244 measuring 33 acres 16 guntas situated at Ravudakunda village, Sindhanur Taluk, Raichur District.

A portion of the said land to an extent of 3 acres 22 guntas was sought to be acquired by issuance of the Notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'the Act') for the purpose of construction of a new railway line till Munirabad- Mahaboobnagar.

sentences.text: The Notification under Section 6(1) of the Act having been issued on 13.06.2011, consent award came to be passed on 03.10.2013 under Section 11(2) of the Act.

However, the land belonging to the petitioner was excluded from the said consent award nor a general award was passed in relation thereto.
4. There being certain disputes as regards title, the petitioner had filed a suit in O.S.No.110/2014 seeking declaration of title and permanent injunction which came to be dismissed.
However, on an appeal being filed in R.A.No.35/2017, the same came to be allowed and decreed in favour of the petitioner.
RSA No.200057/2022 filed by the State came to be dismissed.
5. On the ground that the petitioner's title has been declared and confirmed, the petitioner submitted a representation on 11.04.2023 seeking for awardal of compensation/disbursement of compensation.

The same came to be rejected by the Special Land Acquisition Officer at Annexure-H on the ground that as on the date of the award, the name of the Government was found in the RTC and since the name of the petitioner was not found, no award could be passed in favour of the petitioner.
6. It is rather strange that such a stand has been taken by the Special Land Acquisition Officer.

Though there might have been claims or counter claims or dispute as regards title to a property,
when a notification under Section 4(1) or 6(1) was issued, if subsequent thereto, the issues and/or claims regarding title are adjudicated by the Court of law, the Special Land Acquisition Officer would be bound by any such adjudication by a Court of law.

7. In the present matter, being aggrieved by the entry of the name of the Government in the RTCs,
the petitioner filed a suit in O.S.No.110/2014 seeking for declaration of title and permanent injunction against the State Government.

The said suit though was dismissed, the Regular Appeal filed in R.A.No.35/2017 came to be allowed and a decree was passed in favour of the petitioner declaring the petitioner to be owner of the said land.
On a second appeal being filed by the State, the said appeal came to be dismissed.

Thus, declaration of title of the petitioner has attained finality and this declaration being against the State Government, the necessary consequences would be the requirement for the entry of the name of the State Government in the revenue documents is required to be deleted.
The Special Land Acquisition Officer ought to have taken these factors into consideration and released the compensation amounts by passing necessary general award in favour of the petitioner.
Thus, without doing that, the endorsement dated 15.04.2023 being devoid of merit is required to be quashed.

Hence, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The Writ Petition is allowed.
i i . A c e r t i o r a r i i s i s s u e d , t h e e n d o r s e m e n t b e a r i n g No.A.PA/sC/g/01/09- 10/35 dated 15.04.2023 at Annexure-H is hereby quashed.

iii. A mandamus is issued directing the respondents to pass a general award in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
